_comment: FULL-COVERAGE W-2 test payload: a value for every one of the 78 fields w2_map binds on the Drake 2025 W-2 screen. Its job is mechanical coverage, not tax realism — it exercises every kind (ts, ein, text, state, zip, money, code, year, checkbox) and every repeated block (box 12 a-d, box 14 lines 1-4, state/local rows 1-4, Box 13, and the three bottom flags). See _not_covered below for what is deliberately left out and why.
_city_zip_note: City and ZIP are kept CONSISTENT on purpose. Drake validates the ZIP and rewrites the city to match (75001 is Addison TX, 75201 is Dallas TX) — an inconsistent pair makes the after-screenshot look like a mis-entry when it is Drake being right.
_not_covered: Fields 2 and 3 (F, Special tax treatment) are protected header dropdowns whose typed behaviour is unconfirmed. 11/12/13 and 20/21/22 are FOREIGN-ONLY boxes and 31 (box 9) is greyed out — w2_map refuses to bind all of them. 88 (spouse ITIN) is above the highest confirmed number. Those are the gap between the 78 entered here and the ~88 numbers visible on screen.
_locality_note: Box 20 stores a CODE from Drake's own table (STATELIB\CITY.HLP), not the name printed on the W-2 — that is why 'PHILA'/'NYC'/'MARION' were echoed by the popup and stored by nothing on 2026-08-04. The four rows here deliberately exercise all four ways a real Box 20 string gets resolved: OH 'COLUMBUS' is already the code; IN 'MARION COUNTY' needs the noise suffix cut, then the county NAME maps to numeric code '49'; NY 'NYC' is a curated alias for code 'NY'; PA 'Philadelphia' matches the full name, mixed case, and resolves to 'PL'. Only 11 states are in the table at all (CA DE IN KY MI MO NY OH OR PA) — for anything else the dropdown is genuinely empty and the plan says so instead of typing.
